content.title: About
content.content: Green beans cooked Szechuan-style are tender bean pods quickly stir‑fried with aromatic spices such as Szechuan peppercorns, garlic, ginger and soy sauce. The dish delivers a characteristic spicy‑numbing flavor and a crisp texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Szechuan peppercorns contain hydroxy‑α‑sanshool, which creates a tingling, numbing sensation in the mouth.
Traditionally the beans are cooked only a few minutes to keep them crunchy.
In China the dish is often served as a side to rice or noodles.
Szechuan cuisine is famous for its bold combination of heat and fragrant spices.
Green beans are a good source of plant protein and dietary fiber.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports healthy digestion and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: A serving provides about 35 kcal, making it suitable for weight‑controlled diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B6 and folate, important for metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Provides iron, magnesium and potassium, which support heart and muscle function.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Szechuan pepper and ginger add antioxidant compounds that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Spicy heat
items.content: Excessive Szechuan pepper can irritate the stomach in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Soy sauce allergy
items.content: People allergic to soy should use a soy‑free alternative.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Soy sauce raises sodium levels, so those with hypertension should limit portion size.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot as a side dish with rice, noodles, or incorporate into stir‑fry bowls. Sprinkle with peanuts or sesame seeds for extra crunch and garnish with fresh cilantro.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cooked beans in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat in a pan or microwave with a splash of water to retain moisture.
